newsitem.title: USA: LSI Logic says develops 1.25 gigabit network chip.
newsitem.headline: LSI Logic says develops 1.25 gigabit network chip.

text.p: LSI Logic Corp on Monday said it developed a computer networking chip that enables data to be transferred at 1.25 gigabits, or billions of bits, per second.

Gigabit ethernet is a promising new technology capable of meeting the data-intensive requirements of transmitting voice and video over computer networks. It competes with an alternative technology known as Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM).
LSI said its GigaBlaze single-chip system is capable of meeting the emerging standard for gigabit ethernet networks and is designed to keep pace with the fastest microprocessors currently available.
These include chips from Intel Corp, Motorola Inc, Sun Microsystems Inc and Digital Equipment Corp.

"The introduction of the GigaBlaze G10 core, demonstrates LSI Logic's continued leadership in high speed CMOS serial technology," said Andy Bechtolsheim, vice president of engineering at Cisco Systems Inc's Gigabit Switching Group. "Cisco is using this key technology for next-generation gigabit network switches."

Bechtolsheim, founder of Granite Systems Inc, which was recently acquired by Cisco, is a leading proponent of gigabit ethernet as an alternative to high-speed computer networks based on rival ATM technology.
LSI Logic said it believes GigaBlaze products are the industry's most cost-effective solution for gigabit-scale networking.

The company said its advantage derives from LSI's advanced Complimentary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) process technologies rather than older, multi-chip bipolar or gallium arsenide technologies that have previously been used for high-speed networking.
